classification.difficultyReason: Express the box dimensions using the corner-cut length, form and factorise a quadratic, and reject the physically impossible solution.

content.prompt: A piece of sheet metal $50\text{ cm}\times60\text{ cm}$ has squares cut out of each corner so that it can be bent and formed into a lidless box with a base area of $2184\text{ cm}^2$. Find the length, width and height of the box.

answer.short:
Length $52\text{ cm}$, width $42\text{ cm}$, height $4\text{ cm}$.

Form a quadratic using the base area and reject the cut size that gives negative base dimensions.
answer.worked:
Let $x\text{ cm}$ be the side length of each square cut out. The box has height $x\text{ cm}$ and base dimensions $(60-2x)\text{ cm}$ and $(50-2x)\text{ cm}$, so $0<x<25$.
$$\begin{align*}(60-2x)(50-2x)&=2184\\4x^2-220x+3000&=2184\\4x^2-220x+816&=0\\x^2-55x+204&=0\\(x-4)(x-51)&=0\\x&=4\text{ or }51\end{align*}$$
Reject $x=51$, since it gives negative base dimensions. Thus $x=4$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Length}&=60-2(4)=52\text{ cm}\\\text{Width}&=50-2(4)=42\text{ cm}\\\text{Height}&=4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Check: $52\times42=2184\text{ cm}^2$.
